title: Class XII Economics — Foreign Exchange Rate (Education Beast)
subject: Economics

questions.question_text: Foreign exchange rate refers to:

options.label: A
options.text: the price of gold in terms of the domestic currency

options.label: B
options.text: the price of one unit of a foreign currency in terms of the domestic currency

options.label: C
options.text: the ratio of a country's exports to its imports

options.label: D
options.text: the rate of interest charged on foreign loans

questions.question_text: Under the flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined by:

options.label: A
options.text: the central bank alone

options.label: B
options.text: the market forces of demand for and supply of foreign exchange

options.label: C
options.text: the government of the country

options.label: D
options.text: the World Bank

questions.question_text: Under the fixed exchange rate system, the exchange rate is officially fixed by:

options.label: A
options.text: the commercial banks

options.label: B
options.text: the market forces of demand and supply

options.label: C
options.text: the government / central bank

options.label: D
options.text: the exporters of the country

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a source of demand for foreign exchange?

options.label: A
options.text: Import of goods and services from abroad

options.label: B
options.text: Export of goods to other countries

options.label: C
options.text: Foreign tourists visiting India

options.label: D
options.text: Remittances received from Indians working abroad

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a source of supply of foreign exchange?

options.label: A
options.text: Import of machinery from abroad

options.label: B
options.text: Export of goods and services

options.label: C
options.text: Indian students paying fees to foreign universities

options.label: D
options.text: Indians buying shares of foreign companies

questions.question_text: A fall in the value of the domestic currency in terms of a foreign currency under the flexible exchange rate system is called:

options.label: A
options.text: depreciation

options.label: B
options.text: appreciation

options.label: C
options.text: devaluation

options.label: D
options.text: revaluation

questions.question_text:
A deliberate reduction in the value of the domestic currency by the government under the fixed exchange rate system is
called:

options.label: A
options.text: appreciation

options.label: B
options.text: depreciation

options.label: C
options.text: devaluation

options.label: D
options.text: revaluation

questions.question_text:
A rise in the value of the domestic currency in terms of a foreign currency under the flexible exchange rate system is
called:

options.label: A
options.text: devaluation

options.label: B
options.text: revaluation

options.label: C
options.text: appreciation

options.label: D
options.text: depreciation

questions.question_text: The demand curve for foreign exchange is:

options.label: A
options.text: a horizontal straight line

options.label: B
options.text: downward sloping from left to right

options.label: C
options.text: upward sloping from left to right

options.label: D
options.text: a vertical straight line

questions.question_text:
The exchange rate system in which the rate is mainly determined by the market, but the central bank intervenes to limit
sharp fluctuations, is called the:

options.label: A
options.text: managed floating exchange rate system

options.label: B
options.text: purely flexible exchange rate system

options.label: C
options.text: system of zero foreign trade

options.label: D
options.text: fixed exchange rate system

questions.question_text: In a flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate changes from ₹80 per $ to ₹84 per $. This means the rupee has:

options.label: A
options.text: appreciated

options.label: B
options.text: been revalued

options.label: C
options.text: been devalued

options.label: D
options.text: depreciated

questions.question_text: In a flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate changes from ₹84 per $ to ₹80 per $. This means the rupee has:

options.label: A
options.text: appreciated

options.label: B
options.text: depreciated

options.label: C
options.text: been revalued

options.label: D
options.text: been devalued

questions.question_text: The supply curve of foreign exchange slopes upward because a rise in the exchange rate:

options.label: A
options.text: reduces foreign investment in the country

options.label: B
options.text: makes domestic goods costlier for foreigners

options.label: C
options.text: makes imports cheaper for domestic buyers

options.label: D
options.text: makes domestic goods cheaper for foreigners, so exports increase

questions.question_text: The demand curve for foreign exchange slopes downward because a rise in the exchange rate:

options.label: A
options.text: makes domestic goods costlier for foreigners

options.label: B
options.text: makes imports cheaper, so the demand for foreign exchange rises

options.label: C
options.text: makes imports costlier, so the demand for foreign exchange falls

options.label: D
options.text: makes exports costlier for foreigners

questions.question_text: In a flexible exchange rate system, the equilibrium exchange rate is determined at the point where:

options.label: A
options.text: demand for foreign exchange is more than its supply

options.label: B
options.text: demand for foreign exchange equals supply of foreign exchange

options.label: C
options.text: the government announces the rate

options.label: D
options.text: exports of the country become zero

questions.question_text: If the exchange rate is above the equilibrium rate in a free market, there will be:

options.label: A
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

options.label: B
options.text: excess demand for foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

options.label: C
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will fall

options.label: D
options.text: no change in the rate

questions.question_text: If the exchange rate is below the equilibrium rate in a free market, there will be:

options.label: A
options.text: excess demand for foreign exchange, and the rate will fall

options.label: B
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will fall

options.label: C
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

options.label: D
options.text: excess demand for foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

questions.question_text: Depreciation of the domestic currency is likely to make the country's exports:

options.label: A
options.text: cheaper for foreigners, so exports decrease

options.label: B
options.text: costlier for foreigners, so exports decrease

options.label: C
options.text: unaffected

options.label: D
options.text: cheaper for foreigners, so exports increase

questions.question_text: Depreciation of the domestic currency is likely to make imports:

options.label: A
options.text: unaffected

options.label: B
options.text: costlier in domestic currency, so imports increase

options.label: C
options.text: cheaper in domestic currency, so imports increase

options.label: D
options.text: costlier in domestic currency, so imports decrease

questions.question_text: Appreciation of the domestic currency is likely to:

options.label: A
options.text: increase exports and reduce imports

options.label: B
options.text: have no effect on exports and imports

options.label: C
options.text: reduce exports and increase imports

options.label: D
options.text: increase both exports and imports

questions.question_text:
In a flexible exchange rate system, if the demand for foreign exchange increases while its supply remains unchanged, the
exchange rate will:

options.label: A
options.text: remain unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: fall, i.e. the domestic currency will appreciate

options.label: C
options.text: rise, i.e. the domestic currency will depreciate

options.label: D
options.text: fall, i.e. the domestic currency will depreciate

questions.question_text:
In a flexible exchange rate system, if the supply of foreign exchange increases while its demand remains unchanged, the
exchange rate will:

options.label: A
options.text: rise, i.e. the domestic currency will depreciate

options.label: B
options.text: remain unchanged

options.label: C
options.text: fall, i.e. the domestic currency will appreciate

options.label: D
options.text: rise, i.e. the domestic currency will appreciate

questions.question_text: Which of the following will shift the demand curve for foreign exchange to the right?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase in foreign tourists visiting the country

options.label: B
options.text: Increase in foreign investment in the country

options.label: C
options.text: Rise in domestic residents' preference for foreign goods

options.label: D
options.text: Rise in the country's exports

questions.question_text: Which of the following will shift the supply curve of foreign exchange to the right?

options.label: A
options.text: Indians investing more in foreign countries

options.label: B
options.text: Increase in foreign investment in India

options.label: C
options.text: More Indians travelling abroad

options.label: D
options.text: Increase in India's imports

questions.question_text:
A deliberate increase in the value of the domestic currency by the government under the fixed exchange rate system is
called:

options.label: A
options.text: appreciation

options.label: B
options.text: revaluation

options.label: C
options.text: depreciation

options.label: D
options.text: devaluation

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a merit of the flexible exchange rate system?

options.label: A
options.text: It requires constant government intervention

options.label: B
options.text: The exchange rate never changes

options.label: C
options.text: It ensures complete stability of the exchange rate

options.label: D
options.text: The government need not maintain large foreign exchange reserves

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a merit of the fixed exchange rate system?

options.label: A
options.text: It does not require any foreign exchange reserves

options.label: B
options.text: It adjusts automatically to market conditions

options.label: C
options.text: It is completely free from government control

options.label: D
options.text: It brings stability in the exchange rate, which encourages international trade

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a demerit of the fixed exchange rate system?

options.label: A
options.text: It requires the central bank to maintain large foreign exchange reserves

options.label: B
options.text: It removes the role of the government

options.label: C
options.text: It is determined only by market forces

options.label: D
options.text: The exchange rate fluctuates every day

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a demerit of the flexible exchange rate system?

options.label: A
options.text: It requires large foreign exchange reserves

options.label: B
options.text: Frequent fluctuations in the exchange rate create uncertainty in international trade

options.label: C
options.text: The government must fix the rate every day

options.label: D
options.text: The exchange rate is rigid and cannot change

questions.question_text: Under the managed floating system, if the domestic currency is depreciating sharply, the central bank will usually:

options.label: A
options.text: stop all imports

options.label: B
options.text: sell foreign currency from its reserves

options.label: C
options.text: fix the exchange rate permanently

options.label: D
options.text: buy foreign currency from the market

questions.question_text: Under the managed floating system, to prevent a sharp appreciation of the domestic currency, the central bank will usually:

options.label: A
options.text: ban all exports

options.label: B
options.text: allow the rate to move freely without any action

options.label: C
options.text: sell foreign currency from its reserves

options.label: D
options.text: buy foreign currency from the market

questions.question_text: An Indian student paying tuition fees to a university in the UK creates:

options.label: A
options.text: supply of foreign exchange

options.label: B
options.text: demand for foreign exchange

options.label: C
options.text: neither demand for nor supply of foreign exchange

options.label: D
options.text: appreciation of the rupee

questions.question_text: A US company setting up a factory in India leads to:

options.label: A
options.text: demand for foreign exchange in India

options.label: B
options.text: devaluation of the rupee

options.label: C
options.text: no effect on the foreign exchange market

options.label: D
options.text: supply of foreign exchange in India

questions.question_text: Money sent home by Indians working in Gulf countries is a source of:

options.label: A
options.text: demand for foreign exchange

options.label: B
options.text: devaluation of the rupee

options.label: C
options.text: import of services

options.label: D
options.text: supply of foreign exchange

questions.question_text: An Indian company repaying a loan taken from a foreign bank creates:

options.label: A
options.text: demand for foreign exchange

options.label: B
options.text: no effect on the foreign exchange market

options.label: C
options.text: supply of foreign exchange

options.label: D
options.text: appreciation of the rupee

questions.question_text: For India, ‘foreign exchange’ refers to:

options.label: A
options.text: gold reserves of the RBI only

options.label: B
options.text: Indian rupees held by foreigners

options.label: C
options.text: all currencies other than the Indian rupee

options.label: D
options.text: only the US dollar

questions.question_text:
In a flexible exchange rate system, if India's exports to the USA rise sharply (other things remaining the same), the rupee
will:

options.label: A
options.text: appreciate

options.label: B
options.text: be devalued

options.label: C
options.text: remain unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: depreciate

questions.question_text: In a flexible exchange rate system, if Indians increase their imports of gold (other things remaining the same), the rupee will:

options.label: A
options.text: be revalued

options.label: B
options.text: remain unchanged

options.label: C
options.text: depreciate

options.label: D
options.text: appreciate

questions.question_text: The managed floating exchange rate system is a mix of:

options.label: A
options.text: fixed and flexible exchange rate systems

options.label: B
options.text: two different fixed exchange rate systems

options.label: C
options.text: fixed exchange rate and barter systems

options.label: D
options.text: devaluation and revaluation only

questions.question_text: Under the fixed exchange rate system, if there is excess demand for foreign currency at the fixed rate, the central bank will:

options.label: A
options.text: sell foreign currency from its reserves to keep the rate unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: buy foreign currency to raise the rate

options.label: C
options.text: let the rate rise freely

options.label: D
options.text: do nothing, as the rate adjusts automatically

questions.question_text:
In a flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate changes from ₹80 per $ to ₹88 per $. By what percentage has the
price of one dollar in rupees risen?

An Indian shirt is priced at ₹2,400. If the exchange rate changes from ₹80 per $ to ₹96 per $, the price of the shirt for a US
buyer changes from:

options.label: C
options.text: $30 to $30 (no change)

questions.question_text:
A machine from the USA costs $500. If the exchange rate changes from ₹80 per $ to ₹84 per $, the cost of the machine for
an Indian buyer becomes:

options.label: A
options.text: ₹40,000 (no change)

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): When the rupee depreciates, the demand for Indian exports tends to rise.
Reason (R): Depreciation makes Indian goods cheaper for foreign buyers.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Under the flexible exchange rate system, the government needs to maintain huge foreign exchange
reserves.
Reason (R): Under the flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined by market forces.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): The supply curve of foreign exchange slopes upward.
Reason (R): A rise in the exchange rate makes imports cheaper for domestic buyers.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false.

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.question_text:
Consider the statements:
I. Devaluation takes place under the fixed exchange rate system.
II. Depreciation is a deliberate decision taken by the government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Only I

options.label: B
options.text: Only II

options.label: C
options.text: Both I and II

options.label: D
options.text: Neither I nor II

questions.question_text:
In a flexible exchange rate system, if both the demand for and the supply of foreign exchange increase by the same amount,
then:

options.label: A
options.text: the exchange rate remains the same, but the quantity of foreign exchange rises

options.label: B
options.text: the exchange rate rises, but the quantity remains the same

options.label: C
options.text: the exchange rate falls and the quantity falls

options.label: D
options.text: both the exchange rate and the quantity remain unchanged

questions.question_text: Under managed floating, if the RBI buys US dollars in the foreign exchange market (other things remaining the same), it will:

options.label: A
options.text: increase the demand for dollars and tend to depreciate the rupee

options.label: B
options.text: decrease the demand for dollars and tend to appreciate the rupee

options.label: C
options.text: increase the supply of dollars and tend to appreciate the rupee

options.label: D
options.text: have no effect on the exchange rate

questions.question_text: In a flexible exchange rate system, which of the following combinations will lead to an appreciation of the rupee?

options.label: A
options.text: A rise in Indians travelling abroad and a fall in foreign investment in India

options.label: B
options.text: A rise in India's imports and a fall in India's exports

options.label: C
options.text: A fall in remittances to India and a rise in imports of gold

options.label: D
options.text: A rise in foreign tourists coming to India and a fall in India's imports
